**1. Outside view:** The series has been remarkably stable, oscillating between 29.2 and 30.4 over the past 10 weeks. The mean week-over-week change is 0.31 points. The last reading (29.4) represented a notable 1.0-point drop from 30.4, the largest move in the recent window. A naive extrapolation from the recent average (~29.7) or the last value (29.4) would suggest something around 29.4â29.7.

**2. Inside view:** The 2026 midterms occurred November 3, with Democrats winning control of both chambers â described as a "blue wave." The 11/06 reading (capturing Thursday Nov 5, two days post-election) dropped to 29.4, likely reflecting post-election relief among Democratic voters and Republicans shifting from "angry" toward "discouraged" or "depressed" (the ten-emotion framework means these compete). By 11/20 (capturing Nov 19, over two weeks out), the initial shock is fading. The Reuters/Ipsos poll (Nov 13â16) shows only 27% optimistic, 21% discouraged â suggesting no dominant surge in any direction. Ongoing economic anxiety and the Iran war provide upward pressure on anger, but the political resolution provides downward pressure. Net effect: roughly neutral, maybe a slight drift up from 29.4 as some reversion occurs. I'd estimate +0.1 to +0.2 from the last reading.

**3. Pre-mortem:** If wrong, the most likely cause is underestimating Republican anger consolidation â as the reality of losing Congress sinks in, Republicans may shift from "discouraged" back to "angry," pushing the number toward 30+. Alternatively, continued relief could push it below 29. The smoothing should dampen any sharp swing, but the two-week window allows for meaningful directional movement.

**4. Calibration:** The typical weekly move is 0.31, but we've seen single-week moves up to 1.0. Over two weeks with post-election dynamics, an SD of ~0.6 captures the plausible range (roughly 28.3â30.7) while reflecting genuine uncertainty about which way post-election sentiment breaks.
